name: Ji Kowosòl
english: Fresh soursop juice with milk and nutmeg

ingredients.item: soursop pulp, seeds removed (frozen is fine)

steps: Pull out every black seed from the soursop (they are mildly toxic; never blend them).
Blend pulp with the milk and water until smooth, 1 minute.
Add sugar, vanilla and nutmeg, blend 10 seconds, taste, and add sugar only if needed (ripe fruit needs almost none).
Strain through a coarse sieve if you want it silky. Serve over ice.
batch_tip: Freeze pulp flat in bags on Sunday; a glass is blended in 2 minutes any day.
leftovers: Leftover juice freezes into popsicles the toddler loves.
toddler: Pour his glass before any extra sugar and dilute it half and half with water if it seems strong. Leave out the added sugar completely for him; ripe soursop is already sweet. Check for seeds.
swap: Swap half the milk for plain Greek yogurt and a splash of water for about 6 g more protein per glass.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of creamy ivory-white soursop juice dusted with nutmeg, ice cubes and a few pieces of soursop fruit beside it served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Ji Chadèk
english: Fresh grapefruit juice with ginger and honey
steps: Roll each grapefruit on the counter, halve and squeeze (a hand juicer takes 5 minutes).
Grate the ginger and press its juice out through a sieve.
Stir the juice, ginger juice, honey and water together. Taste: it should be tart, not sharp.
Serve over ice.
batch_tip: Squeeze for 3 days at once; vitamin C holds in a closed jar in the fridge for 3 days.
leftovers: Freeze leftover juice in an ice tray for cooling water or smoothies.
toddler: Dilute 1 part juice to 2 parts water and skip the honey (no honey under 12 months). Grapefruit interacts with some medications, so skip it if anyone takes a statin or blood-pressure medicine.
swap: Replace the honey with a ripe banana blended in for a thicker, filling breakfast drink.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of pink-orange grapefruit juice with a halved grapefruit and a slice of ginger beside it served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Ji Zoranj
english: Fresh-squeezed orange juice
steps: Roll each orange firmly, halve and squeeze. Strain out the seeds; keep the pulp if you like it.
Add the water and squeeze in the lime.
Chill 10 minutes, or pour over ice and serve right away.
batch_tip: Squeeze Sunday night for Monday through Wednesday mornings.
leftovers: Leftover juice is a great marinade base for chicken or pork (add epis).
toddler: Plain and unsweetened; 4 oz is plenty. Strain the pulp if he gags on it.
swap: Add a handful of frozen mango and blend for a thicker pre-workout drink with more fiber.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of a pitcher of bright orange juice with halved oranges and a few mint leaves served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Ji Kawòt ak Bètrav
english: Carrot-beet juice with apple and ginger
steps: Scrub carrots and beets (peel the beets if they are old). Chop everything small enough for the blender.
Blend with the water until very smooth, 90 seconds.
Pour through a fine sieve, pressing on the pulp. Add the lime juice.
Serve cold. Keep the pulp for fritters.
batch_tip: The juice keeps 48 hours in a closed jar. Drink the beet juice 2 to 3 hours before a hard run or lift.
leftovers: Pulp goes into scraps-vegetable-fritters.
toddler: Dilute 1:1 with water. Beets turn his diaper pink or red; that is normal, not blood.
swap: Add 1 tbsp ground flax per glass for omega-3 and fiber, or a scoop of unflavored protein.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of deep ruby-red carrot-beet juice with whole carrots, a beet and apple slices beside the glasses served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Ji Mango
english: Fresh ripe mango juice
steps: Peel and cube the mangoes; scrape the pit well, because the flavor is there.
Blend the mango with 1 cup of water, then stir in the rest of the water and the lime juice.
Taste, and add sugar only if the mangoes were under-ripe.
Serve over ice.
batch_tip: Freeze cubed mango in bags in season; a bag becomes juice in 2 minutes.
leftovers: Leftover juice into popsicle molds.
toddler: Skip the sugar completely. Ripe mango is a great first food; serve in a small open cup.
swap: Blend in 1/2 cup Greek yogurt per glass for a mango lassi with about 8 g protein.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of golden-orange mango juice with fresh mango cubes and a halved lime served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Ji Zannanna
english: Pineapple juice with the peel tea trick
steps: Scrub the pineapple skin well. Cut off the peel and core in thick strips and keep them.
Simmer peel, core, ginger and cinnamon in the water 15 minutes, then strain and cool: this peel tea carries a lot of flavor and costs nothing.
Blend the pineapple flesh with the cold tea until smooth. Strain if you like it light.
Sweeten only if needed. Serve over ice.
batch_tip: The peel tea alone also drinks well chilled; make it while the pot is out.
leftovers: Blend leftover juice with frozen banana for a quick smoothie.
toddler: Dilute 1:2 with water; pineapple is acidic and can irritate his chin. No added sugar.
swap: Use coconut water instead of the water for extra potassium after a run.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of pale-yellow pineapple juice in a jug with cut pineapple rings and a cinnamon stick served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Ji Sitwon / Limonad
english: Lightly sweetened fresh limeade
steps: Roll the limes, halve and squeeze (about 3/4 cup juice).
Stir the sugar with 1 cup of the water until it dissolves.
Add the lime juice, the rest of the water and the salt (it helps rehydration after sweating).
Taste, adjust with water or sugar, serve over ice with mint.
batch_tip: Make a lime-sugar syrup that keeps a week; dilute each glass to taste.
leftovers: Freeze into ice cubes for flavored water.
toddler: Make his glass with half the sugar or none; diluted lime water is fine. Limes can sting a sore mouth, so offer plain water too.
swap: For a post-workout version add 1/4 tsp more salt and 1 tbsp honey per glass.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of pale green limeade with floating lime wheels and ice served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Ji Melon Dlo
english: Fresh watermelon juice with lime
steps: Cube the watermelon and blend with the lime juice until smooth.
Strain if you like it light. Add the pinch of salt (it brings out sweetness and helps recovery).
Serve over ice with mint.
batch_tip: Cube and freeze watermelon: no ice needed and it gets frosty.
leftovers: Freeze leftover juice for popsicles.
toddler: No sugar needed. Great on hot days; offer in an open cup.
swap: Add 1/2 cup tart cherry juice for a recovery boost (citrulline plus polyphenols).
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of bright pink watermelon juice with watermelon cubes and a lime wedge served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Ji Papay-Kawòt
english: Papaya and carrot juice with orange
steps: Peel and cube the papaya; blend with chopped carrots and water until very smooth.
Add the orange and lime juice and blend again 20 seconds.
Strain if the carrots leave grit. Serve cold.
batch_tip: The batch keeps 2 days; papaya turns bitter if blended too long, so keep it under 2 minutes.
leftovers: Freeze leftovers for smoothies.
toddler: Mild and sweet, no sugar needed. Papaya is gentle on digestion, which toddlers often need.
swap: Blend in 1/2 cup Greek yogurt for about 8 g protein and creaminess.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of orange papaya-carrot juice with papaya slices and carrot sticks served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Ji Sorèl
english: Hibiscus (sorrel) drink with ginger, clove and orange peel
steps: Boil 4 cups water with ginger, cloves, cinnamon and orange peel for 5 minutes.
Add the hibiscus, turn off the heat, cover and steep 20 minutes (longer for a deeper flavor).
Strain into a jug, stir in the sugar while still warm, add the remaining 4 cups cold water.
Chill and serve over ice.
batch_tip: It improves overnight and keeps 5 days in the fridge; steep a double batch.
leftovers: Use the spent hibiscus for a second weak steep.
toddler: Make his without sugar and well diluted. Hibiscus is tart and can mildly lower blood pressure; a small cup is fine.
swap: Use 1/4 cup sugar and a squeeze of lime, or sweeten with pineapple juice.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of deep ruby-red hibiscus drink with ice, orange peel and a cinnamon stick served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Jenjanm (Homemade Ginger Beer)
english: Spicy non-fermented ginger beer
portion: Adults 10 oz; toddler none or 2 oz diluted
steps: Scrub the ginger (no need to peel) and blend with 2 cups of the water. Strain, pressing hard.
Boil the strained ginger liquid with the cloves, cinnamon and brown sugar 10 minutes.
Cool, add 6 cups cold water and the lime juice.
Chill and serve over ice; the ginger settles, so stir before pouring.
batch_tip: Make the ginger concentrate (steps 1-2) and keep it in a jar: 1 part concentrate to 3 parts water or seltzer.
leftovers: Leftover ginger pulp goes into tea or stir-fries.
toddler: It is spicy. Offer only a small diluted taste or plain water.
swap: Use seltzer instead of water for a fizzy version without extra sugar.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of amber ginger beer with ice, lime wedges and ginger slices beside the glasses served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Green Juice (Spinach, Pineapple, Cucumber, Lime)
english: Mild green juice with pineapple sweetness
steps: Blend the water, pineapple, cucumber, ginger and lime first.
Add the spinach in two handfuls and blend until smooth, 1 minute.
Taste: it should taste of fruit, not grass. Add more pineapple if needed.
Serve over ice right away.
batch_tip: Freeze the spinach-pineapple mix in cups as smoothie packs.
leftovers: Leftover juice into popsicles.
toddler: Mostly fruit tasting; give 4 oz with a spoon of yogurt on the side. Skip the ginger for him.
swap: Add 1/2 cup Greek yogurt or a scoop of unflavored whey for 12-20 g protein.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of bright green juice with pineapple chunks, cucumber slices and spinach leaves served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Cherry-Beet Recovery Juice
english: Tart cherry and beet juice for after hard sessions
steps: Blend the beets with the water until fully smooth, then strain.
Stir in the tart cherry juice, the orange juice and the ginger juice.
Taste: add water if too tart. Chill.
Drink within 30-60 minutes after a hard lift or run.
batch_tip: Keeps 3 days; make it after the long session or Sunday for the week.
leftovers: Freeze into popsicles for sore days.
toddler: Not for him; tart cherry juice is strong and adds little. Offer orange juice instead.
swap: Add 20 g whey protein to the glass, or a cup of Greek yogurt on the side.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of dark crimson cherry-beet juice with whole cherries and a slice of beet in the glass served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Coconut-Pineapple Electrolyte Drink
english: Coconut water with pineapple, lime and salt for long runs
portion: Adults 16 oz on long runs; toddler 3 oz
steps: Stir the coconut water and pineapple juice together in a jug.
Add the lime juice and the salt; stir until dissolved.
Chill. Sip 8 oz per 30 minutes during a run longer than 60 minutes, or 16 oz in the 30 minutes after.
Shake before serving, since the salt settles.
batch_tip: Pre-mix 3 bottles Saturday night for the Sunday long run.
leftovers: Freeze in ice cube trays for hot-day rehydration cubes.
toddler: Plain coconut water is fine for him; no extra salt and skip the pineapple if his mouth is sensitive.
swap: For heavy sweaters add 1/4 tsp more salt and 1 tbsp honey per quart.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of pale coconut water and pineapple drink in sports bottles and a jug, with lime wedges and a coconut half served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Soursop-Banana Protein Smoothie
english: Soursop, banana and Greek yogurt recovery smoothie
steps: Add the milk and yogurt to the blender first, then the fruit, milk powder and honey.
Blend until smooth, 60-90 seconds; add ice or a splash of milk to adjust.
Dust with nutmeg and pour. Drink within 30 minutes of training.
batch_tip: Bag the fruit with the dry milk powder in freezer bags; add milk and yogurt and blend.
leftovers: Leftover goes into popsicle molds.
toddler: Serve his portion with no honey, in a cup with a straw. Check the soursop for seeds.
swap: Add 1 scoop of unflavored whey for about 25 g protein per glass.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of thick creamy off-white soursop banana smoothie with banana slices, nutmeg and a straw served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Oat-Banana Breakfast Smoothie
english: Oats, banana, peanut butter and milk smoothie
steps: Soak the oats in the milk 5 minutes (or overnight) so they blend smooth.
Blend the oats and milk 30 seconds.
Add the bananas, peanut butter, cinnamon and vanilla; blend 60 seconds until creamy.
Pour into glasses. Add ice if you like it cold.
batch_tip: Soak the oats in milk in the fridge the night before; breakfast takes 90 seconds.
leftovers: Heat leftover smoothie in a pot and it is warm oat porridge.
toddler: Fine as is; confirm there is no peanut allergy history first. Serve thick, with a spoon.
swap: Add 1/2 cup Greek yogurt or a scoop of whey for 12-20 g more protein.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of thick tan oat-banana smoothie in glasses with sliced banana, scattered oats and a dusting of cinnamon served family-style in a tall glass jug with glasses on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Pan-Seared Steak with Garlic Mashed Potatoes
english: Sirloin steak with garlic mashed potatoes
portion: Adults 6 oz steak + 1 cup mash; toddler 2 oz sliced steak + 1/2 cup mash
steps: Salt the steaks and rest at room temperature 30 minutes. Peel and cube potatoes with 4 cloves garlic.
Boil potatoes and garlic in salted water until fork-tender, 15 minutes. Drain and steam dry 2 minutes.
Mash with warm milk and 3 tbsp butter until creamy; keep covered.
Heat a cast-iron pan very hot, add the oil, sear steaks 3-4 minutes a side for medium-rare (130F).
Add 1 tbsp butter and 4 smashed garlic cloves to the pan, baste 1 minute. Rest steaks 8 minutes, slice against the grain.
batch_tip: Cook a double batch of mash for the week. Buy a whole sirloin roast, cut it into steaks and freeze the extras.
leftovers: Slice the cold steak thin for a sandwich with pikliz, or chop it into bistek tomorrow.
toddler: Cut his steak into thumb-sized strips against the grain and cook his piece to medium; no added salt on his portion.
swap: Swap half the mash for roasted broccoli, or stir 1/2 cup Greek yogurt into the mash for about 6 g more protein.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of a sliced medium-rare sirloin steak with a golden crust next to a mound of creamy garlic mashed potatoes served family-style in a enamel plate on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Bistèk ak Zonyon ak Pire
english: Haitian-style steak with onions and mashed potatoes
portion: Adults 5 oz steak + 1 cup mash; toddler 2 oz steak + 1/2 cup mash

ingredients.item: top round or sirloin tip steak, thin

steps: Cut the steak into palm-sized pieces. Rinse with lime and water, drain, and marinate in epis, lime and salt 30 minutes to overnight.
Boil peeled potatoes in salted water 15-18 minutes; drain and mash with warm milk and butter.
Sear the steak in hot oil in two batches, 2 minutes a side. Move to a plate.
In the same pan soften the onions with tomato paste and 1/2 cup water 10 minutes until jammy.
Return the steak to the onions for 2 minutes; add scotch bonnet at the end for the adults only. Serve over the mash.
batch_tip: Marinate the steak the night before. Double the onions: they keep 4 days.
leftovers: Tuck steak and onions into bread with pikliz for lunch tomorrow.
toddler: Pull his portion before the scotch bonnet goes in; cut small and cook through. Mash is his favorite part.
swap: Use lean round steak and replace half the mash with sautéed cabbage on a rest day (about 20 g fewer carbs).
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of thin seared steak strips smothered in glossy golden-brown onions beside a scoop of white mashed potatoes served family-style in a enamel plate on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Steak with Sweet Potato Mash and Green Beans
english: Sirloin steak, sweet potato mash and garlicky green beans
portion: Adults 6 oz steak + 3/4 cup mash + 1 cup green beans; toddler 2 oz steak + 1/2 cup mash + a few beans
steps: Rest the salted steaks at room temperature 30 minutes. Peel and cube sweet potatoes; boil until soft, 15 minutes.
Mash with butter, juice and cinnamon.
Sear steaks in hot oil 3-4 minutes a side; rest 8 minutes.
Sauté green beans with garlic in the same pan 5-6 minutes until bright and just tender.
Slice the steak against the grain and plate with mash and beans.
batch_tip: Roast a tray of sweet potatoes on Sunday and mash them on demand.
leftovers: Chop leftover steak into the mash for a skillet hash.
toddler: Cut the beans short; sweet potato mash is a natural favorite. Cook his steak to medium.
swap: Use frozen green beans to save time and money.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of sliced pink steak resting beside bright orange sweet potato mash and glossy green beans served family-style in a enamel plate on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Sheet-Pan Steak Bites with Roasted Potatoes
english: Garlic steak bites, crispy potatoes and peppers on one pan
portion: Adults 1.5 cups steak and potatoes; toddler 1/2 cup with small pieces
steps: Heat the oven to 450F with the sheet pan inside. Toss the potatoes with 2 tbsp oil, half the paprika and salt.
Roast the potatoes 15 minutes, turning once, while you prep the rest.
Toss steak cubes, peppers, onion and garlic with the remaining oil, paprika, thyme and salt.
Add everything to the hot pan and roast 10-12 minutes until the steak is browned and the potatoes crisp.
Finish with lime and scallions.
batch_tip: Roast a double pan and use half in tomorrow's rice bowls.
leftovers: Pile leftovers into a tortilla with pikliz.
toddler: Cut his steak pieces small and cook through; no black pepper on his portion.
swap: Replace half the potatoes with broccoli to cut carbs on rest days.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of a sheet pan of browned steak cubes, crisp golden baby potatoes and colorful pepper strips served family-style in a white ceramic baking dish on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Steak and Plantain Power Bowl
english: Sliced steak, fried ripe plantains, black beans and rice
portion: Adults 1 full bowl; toddler 1/3 bowl, steak minced
steps: Marinate the steak in epis, lime and salt while you prep (30 minutes).
Slice plantains on the bias; pan-fry in a little oil 2 minutes a side until deeply golden. Drain on paper.
Warm the black beans with a splash of water and a pinch of cumin.
Sear the steak 3-4 minutes a side; rest 8 minutes; slice thin against the grain.
Build bowls: rice, beans, steak, plantains, avocado slices and lime.
batch_tip: Cook the rice and beans Sunday; sear the steak and fry plantains to order.
leftovers: Leftover bowl components make fried rice the next day.
toddler: Mash a few plantain pieces and the beans; steak in tiny strips. Avocado is a great toddler food.
swap: For a rest day halve the rice and double the greens.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of a bowl of white rice topped with sliced steak, golden fried plantains, black beans and avocado fans served family-style in a ceramic bowl on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Budget Chuck Steak with Pineapple-Lime Marinade and Potatoes
english: Tenderized chuck steak, quick-marinated, with garlic potatoes
portion: Adults 5 oz sliced steak + 1 cup potatoes + vegetable; toddler small slices
steps: Poke the steak all over with a fork; marinate with pineapple juice, lime, garlic and salt 2-8 hours (the enzymes tenderize it; do not exceed 8 hours).
Cut potatoes into wedges, toss with oil and roast at 425F 35 minutes.
Pat the steak dry, sear in a hot pan 4 minutes a side or broil 5 minutes a side for medium.
Rest 10 minutes and slice very thin against the grain; thin slices are what make chuck tender.
Steam the broccoli for the last 5 minutes. Serve together.
batch_tip: Chuck goes on sale at $5-6/lb; marinate three steaks and freeze them in the marinade.
leftovers: Slice leftovers for a stir-fried rice bowl.
toddler: Slice very thin or finely chop for him; it can be chewy otherwise.
swap: Flank steak ($8-9/lb) is more tender; chuck eye is the best budget cut.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of thin slices of marinated chuck steak fanned on a plate with golden roasted potato wedges and broccoli served family-style in a enamel plate on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Pire Pòmdetè
english: Creamy kid-friendly mashed potatoes
steps: Peel and cube potatoes; cover with cold salted water.
Bring to a boil and cook 15 minutes until a fork slides in with no resistance.
Drain well and let steam dry 2 minutes, then return to the hot pot.
Mash with the warm milk and butter until completely smooth; add salt to taste.
batch_tip: Make 2 batches: mash freezes flat in bags for 3 months.
leftovers: Form leftovers into patties and pan-fry for breakfast.
toddler: This is his dish: hold the salt for his portion and serve warm, not hot; loosen with milk for a young toddler; leave out garlic and pepper.
swap: For the adults, stir in 1/2 cup plain Greek yogurt and 1 tsp black pepper per batch.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of a mound of creamy smooth white mashed potatoes with a pat of melting butter served family-style in a ceramic bowl on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Pire Patat
english: Sweet potato mash with cinnamon
steps: Peel and cube the sweet potatoes; boil 15-18 minutes until very soft.
Drain and mash with butter and milk until smooth.
Stir in the cinnamon. Taste: it should be naturally sweet.
batch_tip: Roast sweet potatoes whole at 400F on Sunday for the week and mash on demand.
leftovers: Make sweet potato pancakes with an egg and 2 tbsp flour.
toddler: A classic first food: no salt, no sugar; thin with a little milk if he is under 2.
swap: Stir in 1/2 cup Greek yogurt for about 6 g more protein.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of a smooth bowl of bright orange sweet potato mash with a dusting of cinnamon and a pat of butter served family-style in a ceramic bowl on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Pire Pòmdetè ak Legim
english: Mashed potatoes with hidden cauliflower and carrot
steps: Peel and cube the potatoes and carrots; add the cauliflower for the last 8 minutes.
Boil everything in salted water until very soft, 15-18 minutes.
Drain well, steam dry 2 minutes, then mash with warm milk and butter.
For the smoothest mash, use a hand blender 20 seconds; the vegetables vanish.
batch_tip: Cook a big pot; the vegetables vanish in the mash and the batch freezes.
leftovers: Use leftovers as the topping for a shepherd's-pie style dish.
toddler: The vegetables disappear into the potato and the carrot makes it sweeter; keep it very smooth for him and salt-free.
swap: Use half potato, half cauliflower on rest days to drop about 10 g carbs per portion.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of a pale-orange flecked creamy mash in a bowl with a butter pat and a sprig of parsley served family-style in a ceramic bowl on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Pire Pwoteyin (Protein Mashed Potatoes)
english: Mashed potatoes with Greek yogurt and milk powder
steps: Peel and cube potatoes; boil in salted water 15 minutes until tender.
Drain, steam dry 2 minutes, and return to the pot over low heat.
Mash with the butter, then stir in the yogurt and milk powder until creamy.
Season with garlic powder and salt. Do not boil after the yogurt goes in.
batch_tip: Make a double batch and portion into freezer bags; reheat with a splash of milk.
leftovers: Fold into a breakfast skillet with eggs.
toddler: Same dish for him; skip the garlic powder and added salt, and thin with milk if needed.
swap: Use 2 tbsp unflavored whey isolate in place of milk powder for about 12 g more protein.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of a creamy white fluffy mash topped with chopped chives and a pat of butter served family-style in a ceramic bowl on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Labouyi Farin
english: Haitian wheat-flour porridge with spices
steps: Bring 3 cups water, the cinnamon, star anise and salt to a simmer.
Whisk the flour with 1 cup cold water until no lumps remain; pour slowly into the pot, stirring constantly.
Cook 10-12 minutes stirring until thick and the flour taste is gone.
Add milk, sugar, vanilla and nutmeg; simmer 5 minutes more. Remove the spices and serve warm.
batch_tip: Cook a big pot Sunday night and reheat with milk through the week.
leftovers: Slice chilled leftover labouyi and pan-fry like polenta cakes.
toddler: Serve warm, not hot, with less sugar; the spices are mild. Skip the star anise for him if he is under 12 months.
swap: High-protein: stir 1/2 cup nonfat dry milk powder or 2 scoops unflavored whey into the pot at the end, or top each bowl with 1/2 cup Greek yogurt.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of a bowl of creamy beige porridge with a light dusting of cinnamon and a star anise pod served family-style in a ceramic bowl on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Labouyi Avwan
english: Haitian-style oatmeal with cinnamon, vanilla and lime zest
steps: Bring the water, milk, cinnamon stick, salt and half the lime zest to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the oats and simmer 10-12 minutes, stirring often, until creamy.
Remove the cinnamon stick; stir in vanilla, nutmeg and brown sugar.
Serve warm with a little extra milk and the rest of the lime zest on top.
batch_tip: Cook a pot of 4 servings Sunday and reheat with milk; or make overnight oats with the same spices.
leftovers: Press leftover porridge into a pan, chill, slice and pan-fry.
toddler: Mild and creamy; cool well. Skip the sugar for him if he likes the milk.
swap: High-protein: stir 2 scoops unflavored whey or 1 cup Greek yogurt in off the heat, and top with peanut butter.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of a bowl of creamy oatmeal with lime zest, cinnamon and a splash of milk served family-style in a ceramic bowl on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Labouyi Patat
english: Haitian sweet potato porridge
steps: Boil the sweet potatoes with the cinnamon and star anise in the water until very soft, 15 minutes.
Remove the whole spices, then blend or mash the potatoes with their cooking water until smooth.
Return to the pot; add milk, nutmeg, vanilla and brown sugar; simmer 8 minutes, stirring.
Thin with milk if it gets too thick. Serve warm.
batch_tip: Cook extra sweet potatoes at dinner and blend into porridge the next morning.
leftovers: Freeze in muffin cups for toddler breakfast pucks.
toddler: Naturally sweet, so skip the sugar for him; great when cooled to warm.
swap: High-protein: stir in 1/2 cup nonfat dry milk powder or 1 scoop unflavored whey after cooking, or serve with a soft-boiled egg on the side.

name: Labouyi Diri
english: Haitian rice porridge with milk and spices
steps: Rinse the rice. Simmer with the water, cinnamon and star anise, covered, 20 minutes until very soft.
Mash a few spoonfuls against the pot to thicken it.
Add milk, nutmeg and sugar; simmer 10 minutes more, stirring.
Add vanilla off the heat. Serve warm.
batch_tip: Cook extra white rice Sunday and turn it into porridge with milk and spices in 10 minutes.
leftovers: Chill leftovers and eat as rice pudding.
toddler: Soft and gentle; cool well. Keep the sugar for the adults.
swap: High-protein: whisk 2 eggs into the hot porridge off the heat, or add 1/2 cup Greek yogurt and a scoop of whey.

name: Espageti ak Aransò
english: Haitian spaghetti with smoked herring
steps: Boil the herring in water 10 minutes to remove salt; drain, flake off the bones and skin.
Cook the spaghetti in unsalted water until al dente; reserve 1 cup of the water.
Heat the oil, soften the onion and pepper with epis 5 minutes, add tomato paste and fry 2 minutes.
Add the herring and a splash of vinegar; sauté 3 minutes.
Toss with the spaghetti, adding the pasta water as needed. Scotch bonnet on the side.
batch_tip: Soak and flake herring in bulk and freeze 1/2-cup portions.
leftovers: Fry leftover spaghetti in a pan with an egg for breakfast.
toddler: Boil the herring well so it is not salty, and check carefully for fish bones before serving his portion.
swap: Add a drained can of sardines or 2 scrambled eggs for about 10 g more protein.

name: Espageti ak Poul
english: Haitian spaghetti with chicken

ingredients.item: boneless chicken breast or thighs, cubed

steps: Marinate the cubed chicken in 2 tbsp epis, salt and lime for 20 minutes.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente; reserve 1 cup water.
Brown the chicken in oil 6-8 minutes; remove. Soften the onion and pepper with the remaining epis; fry the tomato paste 2 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the bouillon and 1 cup pasta water, simmer 5 minutes.
Toss with the spaghetti and serve; scotch bonnet on the side.
batch_tip: Cook a double batch of chicken and freeze half for fast dinners.
leftovers: Leftovers become a spaghetti-chicken frittata.
toddler: Cut his chicken very small and serve before the scotch bonnet; go light on salt.
swap: Use all breast meat for lower fat; add 1/2 cup grated parmesan at the end.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of spaghetti coated in orange tomato sauce with golden chicken pieces, onion and green pepper served family-style in a wide shallow pasta bowl on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Espageti ak Legim
english: Haitian spaghetti with vegetables and beans

ingredients.item: white or red beans, canned and rinsed

steps: Cook the spaghetti until al dente; reserve 1 cup water.
Heat the oil, sauté peppers with epis 4 minutes, add carrots and cabbage and cook 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, beans and 1/2 cup pasta water; simmer 5 minutes.
Toss with spaghetti and parmesan; scotch bonnet on the side.
batch_tip: Chop all the vegetables Sunday; the sauce keeps 4 days.
leftovers: Scramble leftovers with an egg for breakfast.
toddler: Cook the vegetables very soft; mash a few beans in for him; go light on salt.
swap: Add a pound of sautéed turkey or chicken sausage for about 15 g more protein.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of tomato-coated spaghetti with colorful shreds of cabbage, carrot, pepper and white beans served family-style in a wide shallow pasta bowl on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Bouyi Viv ak Sòs Pwason
english: Boiled sweet potato, potato, green banana and plantain with fish sauce
portion: Adults 1.5 cups viv + 6 oz fish; toddler 3/4 cup viv + small fish
steps: Rinse the fish with lime and water; marinate in 2 tbsp epis and salt 20 minutes.
Boil the peeled plantain and green bananas in salted water 12 minutes, add the potatoes and sweet potatoes for 15 minutes more until tender; drain.
Sauté onion, pepper and the remaining epis in the oil 5 minutes, add the tomato paste and 1 cup water.
Lay the fish in the sauce, cover and simmer 8 minutes until it flakes; add scotch bonnet at the end for the adults.
Serve the sauce over the viv with pikliz.
batch_tip: Boil a large pot of viv and reheat it in the microwave through the week.
leftovers: Flake leftover fish into rice or an omelet.
toddler: Mash a small piece of each viv for him; fish cooked through and flaked; sauce without scotch bonnet; check for bones.
swap: Use baked cod or salmon; add a cup of beans on the side for about 15 g more protein.
photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of a platter of boiled sweet potato, potato, green banana and plantain beside fish in a red-orange onion sauce served family-style in a wide serving platter on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

name: Viv ak Ze ak Zaboka
english: Boiled viv with eggs and avocado
portion: Adults 1.25 cups viv + 3 eggs + 1/3 avocado; toddler 3/4 cup viv + 1 egg
steps: Peel and boil the plantain and bananas in salted water 12 minutes, add the potatoes and sweet potatoes, cook 15 minutes more until tender; drain.
Meanwhile hard-boil the eggs: 10 minutes at a gentle boil, then cool in cold water.
Slice the avocado and squeeze lime over it so it stays green.
Serve everything family-style with pikliz.
batch_tip: Boil a dozen eggs and the viv Sunday; breakfast is ready all week.
leftovers: Mash leftovers with the eggs for a breakfast hash.
toddler: Mash an egg yolk and avocado with a bit of potato; chop the egg small.
swap: Add 1 can of sardines or 3 oz smoked salmon per adult for about 20 g more protein and omega-3.

name: Viv ak Sòs Vyann
english: Boiled viv with a rich beef (or chicken) sauce
portion: Adults 1.5 cups viv + 1 cup sauce; toddler 3/4 cup viv + 1/2 cup sauce

ingredients.item: beef chuck for stew (or boneless chicken thighs)

steps: Cut the beef into 1-inch cubes, rinse with lime and marinate in epis and salt 30 minutes (or overnight).
Brown the beef in oil in a heavy pot 8 minutes; add onions, pepper and tomato paste, fry 3 minutes.
Add 3 cups water and the bouillon; cover and simmer 45-50 minutes until tender (25 minutes for chicken); add carrots for the last 15 minutes.
Boil the plantain and bananas 12 minutes, add the potatoes and sweet potatoes, cook 15 minutes more; drain.
Serve the viv with the sauce; scotch bonnet on the side.
batch_tip: Make the sauce one day ahead; the flavor improves overnight.
leftovers: Use the leftover beef and sauce in sandwiches or over rice.
toddler: Cut the beef very small or shred it; serve a little of each viv, mashed; no scotch bonnet in his portion.
swap: Chicken thighs cook faster and cost less; use sirloin tips for a leaner option; add beans on the side.
